device_identification.how_it_works: Two single-mode waveguides enter separately at left, are brought into close proximity by symmetric S-bends into a parallel coupling region with a small edge-to-edge gap, run parallel over a coupling length L_c where evanescent fields overlap and power transfers between them (cross-coupling ratio set by L_c and gap), then S-bend apart to two separate outputs at right. Power splitting kappa = sin^2(pi*L_c/(2*L_pi)) where L_pi is the beat length set by the supermode splitting, a strong function of the coupling gap.
device_identification.evidence: Per-column raster trace of component.png: two horizontal leads at y-frac 0.065/0.925 on both left and right; S-bends over x-frac 0.16-0.27 and 0.73-0.84 draw them to a central parallel pair at y-frac ~0.446/0.560 which runs flat over x-frac ~0.27-0.73. Two distinct inputs AND two distinct outputs, no 1x2 splitter/combiner => a 2x2 directional coupler, NOT an MZI.

function_knobs.coupling_gap: edge-to-edge gap between the guides in the parallel region — dominant control on coupling strength
function_knobs.coupling_length: length of the parallel section — sets accumulated coupling phase / splitting ratio (the transfer length)
function_knobs.sbend_length: horizontal span of each access S-bend transition
function_knobs.coupling_width_top / coupling_width_bot: waveguide widths in the coupling region
function_knobs.port_separation_in / port_separation_out: center-to-center port fan-out (device is slightly left-right asymmetric in the figure)
function_knobs.input_lead: input straight lead length (output_lead derived to hold the 120um footprint)
function_knobs.bend_taper_peak_top / bend_taper_peak_bo: parametric access-taper: the figure draws the S-bends with a widened stroke peaking mid-bend; modeled as a variable-width taper on each bend

calibration_note: compare_absolute renders the GDS X left-aligned, Y centered, at ABSOLUTE per-axis scale (scale_x=bbox_w_px/120um=15.82, scale_y=bbox_h_px/4um=184.75). X and Y are scaled independently (~11.7x anisotropy), so the device is designed in real microns with total length 120um and total vertical extent ~4um; fractional layout in the figure is what must be matched.

iterations.change_made: initial topology: symmetric directional coupler, constant-width cosine S-bends, symmetric port separation 3.44um, gap 0.12, coupling 55um
fattened guides to 0.38, smaller gap, steeper bends — only traded precision(0.77) for recall(0.83); global width is not the lever
split port separation into in(3.44)/out(3.66) — the figure is left-right asymmetric (output fans wider); thinned guides to cut coupling FP
tried linear-ramp (sharp-knee) S-bends — WORSE; the target bends are smooth (blue sits in the concave armpit), reverted to cosine

diagnosis: bend columns carry 2-3x the pixel mass of the straights and the figure draws the S-bend stroke with a width bulge peaking at ~1.2um, with the top guide consistently ~1.5x fatter than the bottom. Added a parametric access-taper (variable-width bends via segmented extrudes), separate per-guide lead/coupling widths, and Nelder-Mead over the continuous knobs. Constant-width on the exact traced centerline caps at IoU~0.77; reproducing the width profile is required to clear 0.85 (an exact per-point trace reaches 0.956).

verify_knob_response_coupling_length.interpretation: verify_knob_response is MZI-shaped: it checks that lengths.json delta_length_um moves by delta and that area grows by width*delta (one arm extended). Neither applies to a SYMMETRIC 2x2 coupler: delta_length_um is 0 by design (equal arms, no MZI imbalance), and the 120um footprint is pinned so coupling_length trades length against the output leads (coupling widths ~= lead widths => near-zero net area). This is a topology mismatch, NOT an inert knob.

direct_geometry_response.coupling_width_top_+0.200um: layer-(1,0) area 91.485 -> 104.273 um^2 (+12.79), matching ~coupling_length*delta (10.78) plus the bend-taper base term — a function knob moving real geometry, deterministically and as physics predicts
direct_geometry_response.conclusion: the declared knobs drive real geometry (not just reported numbers); the MZI-specific verify_knob_response cannot register it for a symmetric coupler, so the response is shown directly.
